item.title: CISA adds BeyondTrust Remote Support zero day CVE-2026-102764 and Fortinet flaw CVE-2025-61624 to KEV catalog
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity authorities have updated the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog under Binding Operational Directive 26-04 to mandate emergency remediation for two actively weaponized perimeter access flaws. Unauthenticated remote adversaries exploit origin validation and path traversal bugs to achieve root privileges across enterprise remote support servers and security appliances.
The catalog additions feature BeyondTrust Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access authentication bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-102764 carrying a CVSS score of 9.3 alongside Fortinet path traversal flaw CVE-2025-61624. Confirmed threat telemetry indicates Chinese state-nexus group Armory Castle actively exploited the BeyondTrust zero-day for nearly seven weeks prior to disclosure, deploying custom web shells and wiping local system logs. Federal civilian executive branch agencies face a mandatory November 7 compliance deadline.
Subverting privileged remote access gateways exposes internal enterprise subnets and managed endpoints. Because BeyondTrust appliances maintain elevated administrative connections to remote endpoints, an unauthenticated gateway takeover permits threat actors to extract stored vault credentials, execute arbitrary commands, and move laterally across corporate networks.
- Apply official maintenance updates published in advisory BT26-05 across all self-hosted BeyondTrust appliances immediately. - Centralize event log forwarding to off-box SIEM systems to prevent local log deletion routines from destroying forensic evidence. - Restrict public network exposure of BeyondTrust and Fortinet management portals using zero trust access proxies. - Rotate administrative credentials managed within privileged remote access vaults and inspect active user session logs.
Privileged remote access security relies on off-box audit logging and rapid patch execution to ensure administrative gateways remain protected against state-sponsored zero-day exploitation chains. #CodeDefence #BeyondTrust #Fortinet #CISA #KEV #ZeroDay #AuthBypass #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: Hackers use compromised ConnectWise credentials to sign in to 173 Microsoft 365 tenant environments
item.description:
Cloud security incident response writeups published today detail an ongoing supply chain intrusion campaign targeting managed service provider integration accounts. Threat actors compromised administrative application credentials to bypass multi-factor authentication controls across client cloud tenants.
The attack campaign involved the compromise of service credentials associated with ConnectWise Cloud Backup formerly SkyKick. Unauthenticated remote threat actors leveraged the stolen administrative credentials to gain unauthorized access across 173 Microsoft 365 tenant environments globally. Adversaries exploited the elevated service permissions to query user directories, export mailbox contents, and create rogue administrative OAuth application registrations. ConnectWise disabled affected application access tokens while conducting incident remediation.
Subverting managed service provider cloud backup accounts destroys tenant isolation and cloud identity boundaries. Because MSP backup integrations hold elevated delegation permissions across customer cloud environments, stolen application credentials allow threat actors to access client data without triggering account password reset alerts.
- Revoke and rotate all ConnectWise Cloud Backup service principal integration tokens and delegated administrative permissions. - Audit Microsoft Entra ID audit logs across managed tenants for unverified administrative logins or OAuth consent grants. - Enforce strict conditional access policies restricting administrative API calls to trusted IP ranges and compliant devices. - Review service provider partner access relationships and restrict global admin rights across delegated tenant integrations.
Cloud supply chain security requires rigorous partner permission auditing and continuous service principal monitoring to ensure corporate cloud tenants remain protected against supply chain account hijacking. #CodeDefence #ConnectWise #Microsoft365 #EntraID #SupplyChain #IdentitySecurity #CloudSecurity #AppSec

item.title: OpenBSD kernel root exploit chains 37 year old shared memory integer overflow bug
item.description:
Operating system vulnerability research writeups published today detail a local privilege escalation exploit chain bypassing advanced kernel security protections. Security analysts demonstrated full root execution on hardened operating system kernels by combining legacy integer overflow logic with kernel memory bugs.
The privilege escalation exploit targets OpenBSD 7.9 kernel architecture. Security researchers chained a 37-year-old integer overflow in shared-memory handling subroutines with a separate kernel memory corruption flaw. The exploit chain successfully bypassed OpenBSD KARL kernel-address randomization, alongside hardware-enforced SMAP Supervisor Mode Access Prevention and SMEP Supervisor Mode Execution Protection, allowing local unprivileged users to execute arbitrary commands under root privileges. Official kernel errata patches have been released by OpenBSD maintainers.
Subverting secure operating system kernels highlights persistent risks associated with legacy codebases. When local threat actors achieve privilege escalation on secure server hosts, adversaries gain capabilities to disable system logging, unhook security agents, and access protected memory spaces.
- Apply official kernel errata patches published by OpenBSD maintainers across all deployed 7.9 server instances. - Restrict local unprivileged user shell access on critical server hosts to minimize local execution vectors. - Monitor host system audit logs for anomalous shared-memory allocation requests or kernel crash dumps. - Enforce strict file system permissions across system binaries to prevent unauthorized local privilege escalation.
Operating system kernel defense demands continuous legacy code auditing and rapid errata patch application to ensure hardened server platforms remain protected against local privilege escalation exploit chains. #CodeDefence #OpenBSD #Kernel #PrivilegeEscalation #Root #SystemSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement
